inputs.text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, imposing a new requirement that fresh voter registrants must prove U.S. citizenship to cast ballots in state elections. Officials insist the rule applies only to new sign-ups and state races, but this is plainly another tactic to shield entrenched power by erecting barriers that hit hardest on immigrants, working people, and communities of color. These groups already confront deep systemic obstacles rooted in historical exclusion and inequality when trying to secure the needed paperwork. Such institutional moves prioritize concentrating authority over expanding real democratic access for the vulnerable. We have to confront these restrictions directly and demand the structural reforms that actually deliver justice.
